text: Lesson 2 made a Dockerfile fast to rebuild. This lesson makes the image it produces small and safe to ship, by making sure the only things that survive into the final layer stack are what the running application actually needs — not the entire toolchain it was built with.

Compile a Go binary in a single-stage Dockerfile based on golang colon 1.23, and it builds correctly, but nothing in a single-stage build ever removes that base image's layers. The compiler, the standard library source, and every build cache ship right alongside the finished binary, because the final image is still built directly from that same stage.

A multi-stage build gives each phase its own FROM inside one Dockerfile. AS build just labels that first stage so it can be referenced later — the second FROM starts a completely fresh, unrelated base image. COPY --from=build reaches back into the build stage's filesystem and pulls out exactly one file, the compiled binary. Everything else from that stage simply never exists in the final image.

The same pattern pays off without a compiler in the picture at all. A Node build stage runs the full npm ci, including dev dependencies like a bundler, to produce a dist folder. The runtime stage installs only production dependencies from scratch — resolving its own clean dependency tree rather than inheriting one mixed with build-only packages — and copies in just that dist folder.

docker build runs every stage in the file, but only the last FROM determines what a normal build actually tags — pointing --target at an earlier stage name instead lets you build and inspect that intermediate stage directly, without ever shipping it.

Once the shipped artifact no longer depends on the build stage's base image, you're free to pick the smallest, most locked-down runtime base that can run it — a distroless image with no shell and no package manager, giving an attacker with code execution far less to work with. Next lesson connects multiple containers together: real networking and real volumes for a local multi-container app.
